basics.name: Richard Lee Davis, PhD
basics.label: Education Technology Researcher & Data Analyst
basics.summary: Education technology researcher and data analyst with 7+ years experience in quantitative research, learning analytics, and large-scale assessments. Proven track record in managing international research projects, developing innovative assessment tools, and analyzing complex educational data. Seeking to apply strong statistical, technical, and project management skills to the OECD PISA Analyst role to help drive evidence-based educational policy.

work.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
work.position: Assistant Professor (Biträdande Lektor), Division of Digital Learning
work.summary: Leading research lab focused on AI in education and learning analytics
highlights: Research Leadership: Leading a research lab focused on AI in education and learning analytics. Supervise PhD students and research engineers in developing data-driven educational tools. Secured a 2M SEK Digital Futures grant as co-PI to develop AI-driven multimodal learning support tools.

Project Management: Manage project scope, timelines, and a budget of ~€200k; coordinate with partner institutions and stakeholders. Implemented agile project management practices (bi-weekly sprints, milestone reviews) to ensure on-time delivery of research prototypes and reports.

Technical Innovation: Overseeing development of a novel learning analytics platform to capture student coding process data. Introduced data pipelines and analytics dashboards for educators to visualize student progress, aligning with PISA's interest in process data.

Communication: Write grant reports and research papers (e.g., ACM SIGCSE 2025) to disseminate findings. Mentor junior faculty on publishing and grant writing. Lecturing in graduate courses on Data Science in Education.

work.name: OECD - Platform for Innovative Learning Assessments (PILA)
work.summary: Lead designer of experimental computer science assessment for OECD's PILA initiative
highlights: Assessment Design: One of two lead designers of an experimental computer science assessment ('Karel') for OECD's PILA initiative (innovating on PISA-style assessments). Designed an interactive programming task environment to measure problem-solving skills in students.

International Pilot Coordination: Managed pilot implementation in 4 countries (Singapore, Ireland, Netherlands, Brazil) with 500+ 15-year-old student participants. Liaised with national coordinators to administer the assessment and ensure data quality and adherence to OECD standards.

Data Analysis & Reporting: Analyzed response process data and performance outcomes using R. Identified cross-national trends in problem-solving strategies. Co-authored a research paper presenting the results and methodological insights. Delivered a detailed report and presentation to the PILA project leadership, informing future PISA innovative domain assessments.
Technologies: R (tidyverse), Python; Developed custom web-based assessment tasks (JavaScript/HTML5); GitHub for version control.

work.name: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
work.position: Postdoctoral Researcher, Computer-Human Interaction in Learning & Instruction (CHILI) Lab
work.summary: Research on learning analytics and student assessment under Prof. Pierre Dillenbourg
highlights: Educational Data Mining: Conducted research on learning analytics and student assessment. Developed novel methods to analyze student learning processes (e.g., sequence mining of online learning interactions).

Psychometric Research: Pioneered a Variational Item Response Theory (vIRT) model integrating machine learning with classical IRT to improve the accuracy of ability estimation. Received Best Paper Award (EDM 2020) for this work on efficient psychometric modeling.

Tools Development: Co-developed 'Jupyter Analytics,' a learning analytics toolkit for Jupyter Notebooks, enabling real-time collection of student activity data and instructor dashboards. This project, involving collaboration with software developers, resulted in an open-source tool and multiple publications (e.g., ACM SIGCSE 2025).

Leadership & Mentorship: As Co-Executive Director of the EPFL-ETH Joint Doctoral Program in Learning Sciences (2022–2024), organized annual research workshops and training sessions for 20+ PhD students. Mentored doctoral students in research design and analytics methods.

Collaboration: Worked closely with an international, interdisciplinary team (computer scientists, psychologists, educators) and coordinated a European Commission-funded sub-project on AI in education. Contributed to proposals that secured additional funding for the lab.
Technologies: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch); R; JupyterLab extensions; SQL; Git; Linux.

work.name: Columbia University - FabLearn
work.summary: Developed innovative educational technology solutions during COVID-19 pandemic
highlights: Designed and piloted a chatbot-based inquiry learning tool for remote STEM education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Implemented the chatbot and content logic to guide students through inquiry-based science experiments via messaging.
Conducted usability testing with high school students; gathered feedback and iterated on the tool's design. The successful pilot led to an internal Columbia grant (~$100k) to expand the project.
Delivered documentation and a user guide for educators. This consulting project demonstrated adaptability and innovation in developing educational solutions under time-sensitive conditions.

work.name: Bildungsraum Nordwestschweiz (Education Department, Northwestern Switzerland)
work.summary: Evaluation of digital assessment platforms for regional schools
highlights: Commissioned to evaluate two digital assessment platforms (one summative, one formative) for regional schools. Assessed each platform's usability, user experience, and pedagogical effectiveness by reviewing system data and interviewing teachers.

Authored a comprehensive 10,000-word evaluation report with findings and recommendations. Presented results to education officials, highlighting areas for improvement and the platforms' alignment with learning goals.
This experience honed my ability to communicate technical and pedagogical insights to decision-makers, a skill directly relevant to producing clear, actionable reports for PISA stakeholders.
